meta_description: Predictive maintenance that changes the work order: precision and lead time signed per failure mode, verified outcomes in a truth ledger, and planner reliance gated on evidence.

blocks.x: Maintenance scheduled by evidence: failure-mode-driven models instead of anomaly soup, work-order integration that closes the action gap, and verified outcomes that pay down truth debt, predictions that the maintenance team actually schedule against.

Predictive maintenance works when it is failure-mode engineering: for each asset class, the physical failure modes (bearing wear, winding insulation, cavitation), the signals that precede them, and a model per mode with a lead-time target. The value is measured in one number, unplanned downtime, and one honesty metric: how many predictions were true, false, or simply never checked.

The practice spans signal engineering from the sensor fabric, failure-mode libraries, model-per-mode builds with lead-time targets, and the work-order integration that turns a prediction into a scheduled intervention rather than an alert nobody owns.
Below: the failure modes that make predictive maintenance theater, the reference architecture of the evidence loop, and the console that tracks verified outcomes.

widgets.title: The asset intelligence loop — click nodes for the evidence contract

nodes.label: Vibration & current
nodes.detail: Properly sampled streams (rates set by fault frequencies) with sensor-health contracts — the spectra are only as honest as the sampling.

nodes.label: Spectral analysis
nodes.detail: FFT, envelope and band energy per machine class — bearing geometry math (BPFO/BPFI/BSF) defines the fault bands.

nodes.label: Physics features
nodes.detail: Trend features from the spectra (band energies, crest factor, kurtosis) — the ML layer learns on physics, not on raw noise.

nodes.label: Survival & RUL models
nodes.detail: Weibull-family survival and RUL regression with confidence intervals — new assets start with class-level priors.

nodes.label: Alert policy
nodes.detail: Thresholds from P-F interval economics with planner-load accounting — precision published from teardown truth.

nodes.label: Work-order integration
nodes.detail: Predictions become CMMS work orders with the evidence attached — planners see why, not just what.

nodes.label: Teardown feedback
nodes.detail: Intervention outcomes labeled back (what did the teardown find?) — the next model version trains on confirmed truth.

widgets.note: Click nodes for the contract each layer carries. The teardown-feedback loop is where precision compounds — every confirmed fault is a labeled example.

blocks.sub: Failure-mode models, CMMS integration and the truth ledger

blocks.x: Predictive maintenance becomes theater when the model predicts and nothing changes: alarms land in a dashboard, planners keep their PM calendar, and the same failures happen on schedule. The discipline starts from the failure-mode library, named modes per asset class (bearing wear, winding insulation, fouling), each with its own specialized model rather than one general anomaly score, and wires prediction into the CMMS: a prediction above threshold creates a work order natively, with the evidence attached and the planner's disposition requested.

The truth ledger closes the loop: every prediction is dispositioned (act, defer, dismiss), every teardown result is recorded against the prediction, and the program KPIs read downtime, cost and prediction precision per mode, verified outcomes, not alarm counts. Models retrain on verified outcomes (the only labels that matter), and the console reads precision per mode, because a mode-level precision number is what a planner will actually trust with a maintenance window.

items: A model per mode beats one anomaly score for everything.
Work orders created with evidence attached; disposition requested.
Every prediction dispositioned and verified against teardown reality.
The number planners trust with a maintenance window.

Alerts nobody plans against: precision never measured, outcomes never verified, work orders unchanged. The theater ends when every prediction lands in the CMMS as a planned work order and verifies against the truth ledger.
How do you prove predictions are worth acting on?

Precision and lead time per failure mode, signed: bearing wear at 86% with 14 days’ notice is plannable; stiction at 79% with 5 days gets a different response. The gates require both numbers before planners rely on alerts.

The verified-outcome record: every prediction is checked against what the teardown, inspection or failure actually showed, 93–98% verification, and the ledger is the governance artifact the overlay maintains.
Can this work with our CMMS?
Yes, the integration surface names the CMMS, the sensor fabric and the planner’s calendar. Predictions arrive as plannable work orders with their evidence attached, not as dashboard alerts.
What does the maintenance organization inherit?
The predictive loop, the console with verified outcomes as the headline, the gates and the truth ledger, the organization runs on plannable notice, not on alarm fatigue.

blocks.x: Ask what fraction of last quarter's predictions were verified against reality. The diagnostic will build the truth ledger for your worst asset class, and show what evidence-led maintenance would save.
